claims.text: An equiatomic NiCoCrFe alloy is a high-entropy alloy.
The initial NiCoCrFe system encompasses crystalline solid structures and disordered liquid configurations near its fusion point.
A machine-learned interatomic potential trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics data can reproduce solid and liquid free energies of multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
Simulation-based ab initio methods can include anharmonic contributions beyond those arising solely from thermal expansion.
Training an interatomic potential on ab initio MD data explicitly incorporates electron–vibration coupling into that potential.
Adaptive retraining and on-the-fly error detection can identify and correct configurations outside the training domain.
High-entropy alloys may be defined as alloys with at least five constituent elements at near-equiatomic concentrations.
The proposed method is scoped to temperatures from approximately 0.8Tm to 1.1Tm.
ML-driven molecular-dynamics trajectories capture structural fluctuations, thermal vibrations, and local anharmonicity consistently across the solid–liquid phase boundary.
A machine-learned potential rapidly interpolates between sparse ab initio reference configurations.
Adaptive supplementation of underexplored configurations produces thorough sampling of the relevant configuration space.
The proposed ML workflow preserves all key thermodynamic contributions, including vibrational entropy and electron–vibration coupling.
The proposed method will be approximately five times faster than full ab initio MD.
The proposed method will be approximately five times faster than TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will reproduce benchmark free energies within approximately 10 meV per atom.
The proposed method will predict melting temperatures and latent heats close to ab initio MD and TOR-TILD benchmarks.
The cited prior work provides ab initio simulation results primarily for elemental solids.
The cited records provide prior binary-system and TOR-TILD fusion benchmarks.
Accuracy outside the near-equiatomic HEA composition domain or far outside 0.8Tm–1.1Tm remains undemonstrated.
Transferability to rare configurations and complete treatment of subtle electron–vibration coupling remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: NiCoCrFe contains four elements but is labeled a high-entropy alloy, whereas the stated composition constraint and cited definition require five or more elements.
